questions.q:
Which halogen is known to cause the reaction given below?
$\mathrm{X}_2+2 \mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}_2 \mathrm{O}_3 \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{NaX}+\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}_4 \mathrm{O}_6$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The given reaction represents the oxidation of sodium thiosulfate ($Na_2S_2O_3$) to sodium tetrathionate ($Na_2S_4O_6$).

This specific reaction is characteristic of a mild oxidizing agent.

Iodine ($I_2$) acts as a mild oxidizing agent and quantitatively oxidizes thiosulfate to tetrathionate. This reaction forms the basis of iodometric titrations.

$I_2 + 2Na_2S_2O_3 \rightarrow 2NaI + Na_2S_4O_6$

Stronger oxidizing halogens like chlorine ($Cl_2$) and bromine ($Br_2$) oxidize thiosulfate completely to a higher oxidation state, typically forming sulfate ($SO_4^{2-}$).

Therefore, the halogen $X_2$ that causes the given reaction is only iodine.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Potassium permanganate on heating at $573K$ forms potassium manganate.

Statement II: Both potassium permanganate and potassium manganate are tetrahedral and paramagnetic in nature.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but statement II is false
Both statement I and statement II are true
Statement I is false but statement II is true
Both statement I and statement II are false
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The given reactant is phenyl benzyl ether ($C_6H_5-O-CH_2-C_6H_5$).

When it reacts with $HI$, the ether oxygen is first protonated to form an oxonium ion. The cleavage of the ether linkage then takes place.

The $C_6H_5-O$ bond has partial double bond character due to the resonance of the oxygen's lone pair with the benzene ring, making it strong and difficult to break. On the other hand, the $O-CH_2$ bond is a weaker single bond. Moreover, cleavage of the $O-CH_2$ bond can proceed via a highly stable benzyl carbocation (in an $S_N1$ mechanism) or undergo facile $S_N2$ attack by the iodide ion ($I^-$) at the less sterically hindered and activated benzylic carbon.

Therefore, the $I^-$ ion attacks the $CH_2$ group, cleaving the $O-CH_2$ bond. The products formed are phenol ($C_6H_5OH$) and benzyl iodide ($C_6H_5CH_2I$).

Statement I claims the products are benzyl alcohol and iodobenzene, which is incorrect. Thus, Statement I is false.

Statement II claims that the $-O-CH_2-$ bond is cleaved to give the product, which is correct. Thus, Statement II is true.

Answer: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.q: When a solution of mixture having two inorganic salts was treated with freshly prepared ferrous sulphate in acidic medium, a dark brown ring was formed whereas on treatment with neutral ${FeCl}_{3}$, it gave deep red colour which disappeared on boiling and a brown red ppt was formed. The mixture contains
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution: The brown ring test is a typical nitrate test that involves adding iron(II) sulphate to a nitrate solution, then slowly adding strong sulfuric acid until the acid forms a layer below the aqueous solution. The existence of the nitrate ion will be shown by the formation of a brown ring at the junction of the two layers. Dark brown ring is formed in the confirmatory test of ${NO}_{3}^{-}$ − ions. Deep red precipitate~with ${FeCl}_{3}$ is formed in the presence of ${CH}_{3}{COO}^{-}$ ions.

questions.q: The spin-only magnetic moment value of the compound with strongest oxidizing ability among ${MnF}_{4}, {MnF}_{3}$ and ${MnF}_{2}$ is_____~$B . M$& (nearest integer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The change from Mn3+ to Mn2+ results in the half-filled (d5 ) configuration which has extra stability.So, MnF3 has most oxidising tendency.

Hence,& ${MnF}_{3}$~has the strongest oxidizing ability as it undergoes reduction readily.

Spin only magnetic moment is calculated using the following formula

$\mu = \sqrt{n\left(n + 2\right)}B . M$

$\mu = \sqrt{4\left(4 + 2\right)} = \sqrt{24} = 4 . 89 = 5B . M$

questions.q: In Chromyl chloride, the oxidation state of chromium is $\left(+\right)$ ___________.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The chemical formula of Chromyl chloride is ${CrO}_{2}{Cl}_{2}$. The oxidation state of chromium in chromyl chloride (${CrO}_{2}{Cl}_{2}$) is $+ 6$.

Let the oxidation number of Chromium be “$x$”, the oxidation state of oxygen is $- 2$, the oxidation state of chlorine is $- 1 .$

Then,

$x + 2 ( - 2 ) + 2 ( - 1 ) = 0$

$x - 6 = 0x = 6$
